They play the same eight bars over and over, and the fiddle sighs at every wrong note.|The fiddle next door has got as far as the sixteenth bar. It still sighs, but less.|The piece next door is almost a piece now. You know it as well as the player does, wrong notes included.} {You were trying to read.|It's late, and the wall is thin.|{season == "winter": The radiator carries it into your room like a second instrument.|The windows are open, and half the corridor can hear it.}} Knock and offer to help {You knock. The player is a mortified first-year who has never had a lesson. You hum the eight bars properly until they have them, which is well past midnight.|You knock, and stay to count the beat for an hour. The sixteenth bar comes right for the first time; you both cheer, and the neighbours bang on the wall.|The door's already open when you knock. You tap out the tricky bit on the tabletop while they follow. Bed is very late.} Pillow over your head {You read with a pillow pressed to one ear. You get through the chapter; the eight bars get into your dreams.|You work through it while the fiddle sighs at the sixteenth bar every four minutes, regular as a clock. You finish your reading through gritted teeth.|You study to the sound of it, grudgingly. Annoyingly, it helps; you'll be humming it in the exam.}
